one_liner: Scalar, BSL-licensed C++11 mixed-radix FFT for arbitrary lengths; beats FFTW_ESTIMATE at some awkward sizes, loses elsewhere.
what_it_does: OFFT computes 1-D and multi-dimensional complex FFTs of any length in float or double, with arbitrary strides for interleaved multi-channel data. You construct an offt::Fourier<valueT, depth> object for a given length or dimensions (this precomputes the plan and twiddles), then call Transform(dst, dstStride, src, srcStride) or InverseTransform(). It is its own API, not FFTW-compatible, and is out-of-place only, with no real-input transforms.
how_it_is_fast: It runs an out-of-place, decimation-in-time mixed-radix Cooley-Tukey driver over code-generated straight-line kernels for factors up to 32. Primes 3-31 use Rader's algorithm with Winograd cyclic convolutions, composites such as 6, 10, 12 and 15 use the Good-Thomas prime-factor decomposition, and 8, 16 and 32 use split-radix. Larger prime factors go through a general Rader algorithm with an FFT-based cyclic convolution, so run time stays O(n log n) for any n, and twiddles are precomputed in compact storage. There is no SIMD; its wins come at lengths with large or awkward prime factors, where FFTW_ESTIMATE plans are weak.
when_to_use: Complex FFTs at awkward lengths with large prime factors (e.g. 1025, 4097, 16385, 262145, 16777217) where you cannot afford FFTW_MEASURE planning: OFFT beat FFTW_ESTIMATE with SIMD at 10 of 30 such sizes on the author's machine.
Projects that need a permissive (Boost Software License), dependency-free FFT and cannot ship FFTW under GPL or install Intel MKL.

Portable scalar code for any C++11 platform, including targets without SSE/AVX, where FFTW's SIMD advantage disappears (OFFT beat scalar FFTW_ESTIMATE at 25 of 30 awkward sizes, derived from page data).
Multi-dimensional or strided transforms on interleaved data such as stereo audio or RGB planes, with a choice of DFT sign and scaling convention.
when_not_to_use: Powers of two or ten: SIMD FFTW_ESTIMATE and 1-core MKL are about 1.4-4.2x faster on the author's table (derived from page data; 1024: 2.1 vs 0.5 ns per n ln n for both).
Throughput on modern AVX/AVX-512 hardware: OFFT has no SIMD, and the benchmark machine was an SSE4-only laptop the author calls 'pretty ancient'; he expects the SIMD gap to be larger on newer CPUs.
Real-valued signals, in-place transforms or split real/imaginary arrays: none have a public API yet (README known limitations).
Sizes with a prime factor that does not fit in 32 bits fail, even on 64-bit targets.
When you need a stable API or active maintenance: version 0.3.0 (June 2023), the API may change between minor versions, 3 stars, last commit 2024-05-12 (.clang-format only).

integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (target_compile_features cxx_std_11; GCC builds force -std=c++11), CMake 3.10; Visual Studio 2017 solution, VS2013 via toolset v120; benchmarked with MSYS2 GCC 12.2.0
integration.platforms: any (platform-independent scalar C++11; no SIMD paths)
integration.thread_safety: Use one Fourier object per thread: Transform() and InverseTransform() are const but lazily allocate and write a mutable scratch buffer (mTemp in fourier_base.cpp), so concurrent calls on one object race. Each object owns its own storage; no other thread-safety notes are documented.

gotchas: The default convention FourierParameters{1,1} computes the forward transform with e^(+2 pi j ik/N), the opposite sign to FFTW's forward transform; pass offt::FourierParameters::FFTW ({1,-1}) to match FFTW. Inverse is scaled by 1/N by default.
Source and destination must differ (no in-place); data must be std::complex<float/double>, interleaved.
Thread-safety trap: the transform methods are const yet mutate internal scratch memory (see thread_safety); ReleaseTemp() frees it and the next call reallocates.
The constructor throws (std::invalid_argument for a bad sign parameter; the element-count product throws on overflow), so wrap construction if your code is exception-free.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick OFFT over FFTW when GPL or MKL licensing is a blocker and your sizes are prime-heavy. For speed on regular sizes, prefer SIMD libraries such as PocketFFT (C++ branch), pocketfft-tuned or VectorFFT; OFFT has no head-to-head numbers against them.
verified_claims_summary: First-party table (doc/OfftSpeedComparison.md, v0.3.0): MSYS2 GCC 12.2.0 on Windows 10, Intel i5-2450M (SSE4 only), against the official FFTW 3.3.5 Windows DLLs with FFTW_ESTIMATE (with and without SIMD) and oneMKL limited to 1 or 2 threads, in ns per n ln n. OFFT wins 10 of 30 non-power-of-two sizes against SIMD FFTW (best 16777217: 8.7 vs 12.3, 1.41x) and 12 of 30 against 1-core MKL, but loses at every power of two and ten; optimization flags are not stated, and the FFTW/MKL comparison harness is not in the repo (examples/benchmark links only OFFT).
status_note: Stale one-person project (v0.3.0 June 2023, last commit May 2024, 3 stars, CI self-test on GitHub Actions) under the Boost Software License; small enough to vendor, but treat the API as unstable.
